description: Soft-tissue infected diabetic wound (open wound) pathways. Mapped from DKR infected_diabetic_wound.json (id diabetic_wound_infection); TUH-Inc. Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy Recommendations ver 2025-04-02. This is not the osteomyelitis category in bone_joint.json. Patients with diabetes who have cellulitis but NO open wound should be managed as Skin/Soft Tissue Infection (ssti.json).

mild.description: Mild infection, no recent antibiotic use

severe.description: Severe infection with severe sepsis or septic shock

categories.category: Mild Infection, no recent antibiotic use

regimens.reasoning: Vancomycin for mild infected diabetic wound without recent antibiotic use (TUH 2025-04-02). Same DKR regimen for none / mild PCN / severe PCN.
regimens.evidence: TUH-Inc. Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy Recommendations ver 2025-04-02
regimens.note: For vancomycin allergy, daptomycin IV can be substituted. Patients with NO systemic signs/symptoms of infection and pending biopsy: consider monitoring off antibiotics until biopsy.

regimens.reasoning: DKR lists the same vancomycin regimen for mild PCN allergy
DKR lists the same vancomycin regimen for severe PCN allergy
Ceftriaxone plus vancomycin for moderate infected diabetic wound without severe sepsis (TUH 2025-04-02)
regimens.evidence: TUH-Inc. Empiric Antimicrobial Therapy Recommendations ver 2025-04-02
regimens.alternative: daptomycin IV in place of vancomycin if vancomycin allergy

regimens.reasoning: Ceftriaxone safe for mild PCN allergy; plus vancomycin
regimens.alternative: daptomycin IV in place of vancomycin if vancomycin allergy

regimens.reasoning: Vancomycin plus aztreonam plus metronidazole for severe PCN allergy
regimens.alternative: daptomycin IV in place of vancomycin if vancomycin allergy
regimens.note: If patient has a history of SJS/DRESS, use vancomycin and consult Infectious Diseases for guidance on gram-negative coverage.

de_escalation.criteria: Duration depends on the causative pathogen and clinical scenario.
de_escalation.note: Patients with diabetes who have cellulitis but NO open wound should be managed as SSTI. Patients with NO systemic signs/symptoms of infection and pending biopsy: consider monitoring off antibiotics until biopsy. Consult infectious diseases if assistance needed.
